label: Fact
headline: Sample: Fictional Veldmark parliament delays placeholder budget vote by one week
dek: A sample article showing how {{name}} separates confirmed facts, attributed claims and open questions. Veldmark is a fictional country.
whatHappened: The parliament of Veldmark, a fictional country used for this sample, voted to postpone a placeholder budget vote from 10 November to 17 November 2026 (sample dates).
The postponement motion passed by a placeholder margin of 101 to 87, according to the sample parliamentary record linked below.
whyItMatters: In this sample, the delay pushes the fictional budget past a placeholder fiscal deadline, which would show readers how a procedural vote can carry real consequences.
confirmed: The vote was rescheduled to 17 November 2026 (sample record).

attributed.claim: The delay was needed to finish a placeholder cost review.
attributed.attributedTo: the fictional Veldmark Finance Ministry, in a sample statement

attributed.claim: The delay is a stalling tactic.
attributed.attributedTo: a fictional opposition group, in a sample press release

unknown: Whether the placeholder cost review will be published before the new vote date.
Whether the fictional fiscal deadline can be extended.

changelog.note: Added the placeholder vote margin from the sample record.

corrections.note: Sample correction: an earlier version gave the new vote date as 16 November; the sample record says 17 November.

pullQuote: A procedural vote can carry real consequences when it pushes a budget past a deadline.
